disease_label_per_paper: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (clinical diagnosis, 5/8 HLH-2004 criteria) in a 9-year-old girl with refractory fever
presentation_summary: 9-year-old girl (25 kg) admitted to a tertiary care facility in Pakistan with high-grade fever (104 F) persisting for more than 2 weeks, preceded by a 1-2 month relapsing period of intermittent fever; cough, chest congestion, poor oral intake, fatigue, and pallor.
Fever persisted despite 2 weeks of empiric intravenous meropenem, piperacillin-tazobactam, linezolid, and vancomycin.
Exam: conscious but irritable, mild pedal edema, liver 3-4 cm and spleen 4-5 cm below the costal margin, bilateral crepitations without pleural effusion, unremarkable neurological examination.

Hospital day 1 labs: Hb 8.4 g/dL, microcytic hypochromic indices, WBC 8.5 x10^9/L with neutrophils 7.3% and monocytes 53.4%, platelets 114 x10^9/L, triglycerides 349 mg/dL, fibrinogen 107 mg/dL, ferritin 1144 ng/mL, albumin 2.3 g/dL, ALT 70 U/L, AST 74 U/L, ALP 239 U/L, total bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL; hyponatremia noted.
Imaging: ultrasound hepatosplenomegaly with mild pericholecystic and pelvic free fluid; chest X-ray normal; brain MRI mild atrophic changes and paranasal sinus mucoperiosteal thickening.

outcome.source_text_value: Although the patient received vigorous supportive care, her condition did not improve significantly, and she was transferred to a tertiary care center for further evaluation.

quality_warnings: Only one vital sign (temperature) is reported at presentation; hospital day 1 laboratory table provides the remaining quantitative presentation evidence.
HLH diagnosis is clinical (HLH-2004 5/8) without bone marrow, NK activity, sIL-2R, or genetic testing; the trigger was not identified.
Differential counts converted to absolute counts using the reported WBC; conversions recorded per item.
Hepatic and splenic edge distances are recorded as range midpoints; ultrasound spleen length 15.9 cm is record-only because its timing is not stated.
Autoimmune/infectious exclusion serologies, blood culture result, and the final HLH-criteria adjudication are non-ranking.
